haiku-low.q1: Only the latest missed fire time gets a run once workers recover. Older fire times are dropped with no history row.
haiku-low.q2: The new fire time is recorded as a run with status skipped, finished_at set and no attempts. Nothing executes.
haiku-low.q3: Tried 3 times total, waiting 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2. Then the run is failed, with attempts and errors kept in history.
haiku-low.q4: After the lease expires, at most 2 minutes after the worker dies. The reaper marks the attempt lost and retries if attempts remain. Yes, it uses up one attempt.
haiku-low.q5: The running job finishes normally. Pending runs, including retries waiting to start, become cancelled. On resume, next_fire_at is recomputed to the first fire time after now, so missed fire times are not caught up.
haiku-low.q6: The row lock (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) lets only one worker take the schedule. The UNIQUE (schedule_id, scheduled_for) constraint allows at most one run per fire time.
haiku-low.q7: In job_schedule.next_fire_at. It changes after each run-creation pass, on schedule save or cron/timezone edit, and on re-enable or tenant resume.
haiku-low.q8: In one transaction, the worker selects a pending run with not_before <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, sets it running, adds 1 to attempt_count and inserts an attempt row.
haiku-low.q9: In job_run.lease_expires_at, pushed to now plus 2 minutes every 30 seconds. Every worker's reaper step finds running runs whose lease expired.
haiku-low.q10: The wait is recorded in job_run.not_before with status pending. A worker's claim step starts the retry once not_before <= now().
haiku-low.q11: Once per fire time: a job_run row. Once per execution try: a run_attempt row.
haiku-low.q12: The fencing check: the finish write only applies WHERE status='running' AND attempt_count matches its attempt. If no row changes, it rolls back and cannot overwrite.

sonnet.q1: Only the most recent fire time at or before now gets a run (pending, not_before = now). The two older missed fire times are dropped with no history row.
sonnet.q2: A run for that fire time is inserted with status `skipped` (finished_at set, no attempts) because the schedule already has a run in progress. Nothing executes.
sonnet.q3: Up to 3 attempts. Wait is 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2. If attempt 3 fails, the run ends as `failed`, with 3 attempts and their errors in history. (If the schedule is disabled or tenant paused meanwhile, it ends `cancelled` instead.)
sonnet.q4: Once its lease (now + 2 min, extended every 30 s) expires, i.e. at most about 2 minutes after the last heartbeat, a reaper in any worker marks the attempt `lost` and the run goes back to pending with backoff (1 min after attempt 1, 5 min after attempt 2) if attempts remain. Yes, it uses up one of the 3 attempts, since the attempt was counted at claim.
sonnet.q5: The executing job is left alone and finishes normally (running runs are not cancelled by a pause). The waiting pending run (including one waiting to retry) is set to `cancelled`. During the pause step 2 only selects schedules of active tenants, so no runs are created. On resume, next_fire_at is recomputed as the first fire time after now, so fire times during the pause are not caught up.
sonnet.q6: Step 2 locks the schedule rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so the second worker skips the locked schedule. Also UNIQUE (schedule_id, scheduled_for) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means only one run per fire time.
sonnet.q7: In job_schedule.next_fire_at. It is set when a schedule is saved (first fire time after now), recomputed when cron or timezone is edited, set to the first fire time after now by step 2 each time runs are created, and recomputed on re-enable of a schedule or resume of a tenant.
sonnet.q8: In one transaction it selects one pending run with not_before <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (locked rows are skipped), sets status running, increments attempt_count, sets the lease, and inserts the run_attempt row. Fencing check on later writes also protects.
sonnet.q9: In job_run.lease_expires_at (set only while running), extended by worker heartbeats every 30 s. The reaper step, run by every worker each loop, notices runs with status running and lease_expires_at < now().
sonnet.q10: In job_run.not_before, set to now plus 1 minute (after attempt 1) or 5 minutes (after attempt 2), with status back to pending. The retry starts when a worker's claim step (step 3) finds the pending run with not_before <= now() on a later loop.
sonnet.q11: Once per fire time: a job_run row (unique on schedule_id + scheduled_for). Once per execution try: a run_attempt row (unique on run_id + attempt_no), recording worker, start, end, outcome and error.
sonnet.q12: The fencing check: its finish update says WHERE id = ? AND status = 'running' AND attempt_count = its attempt number. Since the run was reclaimed (attempt_count changed), no row changes, the transaction rolls back, and the worker stops. It cannot overwrite the new outcome.
